correctness.rationale: For m>=r>=3 and s_i>=1, root link faces contain at most r−1 branch centers, so a missing branch provides an isolated distinguished leaf. The least-missing-center leaf toggle is a perfect augmented-face matching; any directed Hasse cycle would preserve its center set and then cannot remove the toggled leaf, proving acyclicity. The link is contractible and root deletion is a homotopy equivalence. The deleted graph is a disjoint union of m stars; Ind_r(K_{1,s_i}) is the suspension of the (r−2)-skeleton of the leaf simplex, giving B=prod_i binom(s_i−1,r−1) spheres in dimension rm−1, including s_i<r contractibility. Its natural integral cycles identify with wedge^(r−1) of the augmentation lattice U_i; join swaps contribute (-1)^r, and the uniform wreath representation is irreducible since its restriction to the normal base subgroup is an external product of irreducible hook Specht modules. Character factors are traces of leaf monodromy around branch cycles. Independently counted 4,679 faces and reduced Euler rank 1 for (r,m,s)=(3,3,3) and 27,667 faces and Euler rank 27 for (3,3,4); source verifier was read and checks link acyclicity, finite-field Betti ranks and signed character samples/full small group. These finite checks corroborate but do not prove the family.
